en: Formerly, there was no one whose teacher could be more venerable than he, whose form was the very ornament of the earth;
yet today that very land, though dear to you, stands beneath all other lands as something to be discarded. (1)
In former times, your city Ayodhyā was more pure than even the city of the gods; now, seeing it overrun by barbarians, our heart is pained—tell me, O fair-minded one, why is this so?
Long ago, when the earth was overrun by the gods, why was that suffering not dispelled by you?
Where is that strength of yours now; alas, why do you not slay the one who strikes cows with a harsh arrow?
I believe that Rāvaṇa, the perpetrator of a multitude of great evils, has indeed been slain by you alone;
why then do you not see those of his kind here today, or are you afraid just as we are? (4)
Sītā was seized by the ten-necked Rāvaṇa, yet she has been recovered by you; there is peace here, no division.
Today, wicked women of various strengths carry away our horses; there is compassion here, but there is sorrow. (5)
Otherwise, O Cloud of Compassion, if you do not show mercy now, though you are truly a friend to the distressed, you manifest cruelty;
to whom else shall this land of Bhārata turn for refuge today? O Delight of the World, dark as a rain-cloud, you yourself must tell us.
The hymn composed by Śrī Rājamaṇiśarman, "Tvameva Brūhi," is hereby complete.
